result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.cmty_walktrap()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Detect communities using Walktrap random walk algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11355-L11502){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.cmty_walktrap(steps=4, attr_name=None, return_dict=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The Walktrap algorithm exploits the property that random walks tend to stay trapped within densely connected communities. It computes distances between nodes based on random walk probabilities, then uses hierarchical clustering to identify community structure. Works only with undirected graphs. Time complexity is `O(n²log n)` for typical networks with small step parameter. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [steps]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[4]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of random walk steps. Higher values capture longer-range structural patterns. Typical values: 2-8. - steps=2: Local structure only - steps=4: Good balance (default, recommended) - steps=6+: Longer-range patterns, more computation [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store community assignments in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `cmty_walktrap`. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to community IDs (0-indexed, contiguous). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on a directed graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Algorithm steps: 1. compute transition probability matrix `P` (`P[i][j] = 1/deg(i)` if edge exists) 2. compute t-step transition probabilities `P^t` by matrix exponentiation 3. calculate random walk distance between each pair of nodes: `d(i,j) = sqrt(Σ_k [(P^t_ik - P^t_jk)^2 / deg(k)])` 4. apply Ward's hierarchical clustering on the distance matrix 5. cut the dendrogram at the level that maximizes modularity The step parameter controls the scale of community detection: - lower steps (2-3): Detect finer, more local communities - higher steps (5-8): Detect coarser, more global communities The algorithm is deterministic (no randomness despite the name). Works well on hierarchical community structures and handles disconnected components automatically. Performance degrades on very large graphs (>10,000 nodes) due to `O(n²)` distance matrix computation. Self-loops and multi-edges are currently not supported. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Detect communities with default parameters: ::: {#0ac95b74 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_node(label="E") .add_node(label="F") ) # Two cliques connected by a bridge for i, j in [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]: graph.add_edge(i, j) for i, j in [("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]: graph.add_edge(i, j) graph.add_edge("C", "D") # Bridge communities = graph.cmty_walktrap(return_dict=True) node_a = graph.get_id_from_label("A") node_b = graph.get_id_from_label("B") node_c = graph.get_id_from_label("C") node_d = graph.get_id_from_label("D") assert communities[node_a] == communities[node_b] == communities[node_c] assert communities[node_d] == communities[graph.get_id_from_label("E")] # Try different step lengths for different scales local_cmty = graph.cmty_walktrap(return_dict=True, steps=2) # More local communities global_cmty = graph.cmty_walktrap(return_dict=True, steps=6) # More global communities ``` ::: Store as node attributes and chain: ::: {#3964f8f6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_node(label="E") .add_node(label="F") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="A") .add_edge(source="C", target="D") .add_edge(source="D", target="E") .add_edge(source="E", target="F") .add_edge(source="F", target="D") ) ( graph .cmty_walktrap(attr_name="community") .colorize_node_attrs(node_attr_from="community", palette="tab10") .describe() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Number of nodes : 6 Number of edges : 7 Directed : False Density : 0.47 Average degree (min, max) : 2.33 (2, 3) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : False Bipartite : False Computations on nodes: - cmty_walktrap() -> attr: 'community' (6 of 6 nodes) Node aesthetics: - color <- community via colorize (palette: "tab10") (values: #1f77b4, #ff7f0e, 6 of 6 nodes) ``` ::: :::
